recognize_zh: 箭頭所指的骨髓顆粒球前驅細胞，細胞質內有明顯比正常顆粒大很多的巨大包涵顆粒（上方細胞為粉紅至紅色大顆粒、左下帶狀核細胞為深色桿狀包涵體），符合 Chediak-Higashi 症候群的巨大溶酶體顆粒。
features: Myeloid precursors containing giant, round cytoplasmic granules much larger than normal primary/secondary granules
Top cell (promyelocyte/myelocyte): several discrete pink-red giant granules clustered at one side of the cytoplasm
Middle cell (myelocyte): coarse grayish inclusion within granular cytoplasm
Lower-left band/metamyelocyte: dark elongated inclusion in pale cytoplasm
Otherwise normal-appearing nuclear maturation; background red cells and platelets
describe_en: Bone marrow aspirate smear shows maturing granulocytic precursors with normal nuclear maturation. Several precursors contain abnormally large, discrete cytoplasmic granules and inclusions, including clusters of pink-red giant granules in a promyelocyte/myelocyte and an elongated dark inclusion in a band form. The inclusions are markedly larger than normal azurophilic or specific granules. No blasts are increased in this field. Findings are consistent with giant granules of Chediak-Higashi syndrome.

ddx.vs: Morphology is similar, but pseudo-Chediak-Higashi granules occur in a clonal myeloid neoplasm with increased blasts/dysplasia and the patient lacks oculocutaneous albinism or LYST mutation.
Alder-Reilly granules are diffuse, dark, fine-to-coarse granules filling the cytoplasm of all granulocytes and lymphocytes, not a few discrete giant granules.
Toxic granules are small, evenly distributed dark granules in neutrophils, not large single inclusions.
These are pale blue peripheral cytoplasmic RNA inclusions (with giant platelets in MYH9 disorders), not pink-red lysosomal granules.
